newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Loewen confused by bid strategy.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Loewen confused by bid strategy.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc chief executive officer Ray Loewen said he is confused by the strategy being followed by Service Corp International, which earlier Wednesday launched a hostile takeover of the Canadian operator of funeral homes and cemeteries.

"I find it interesting. Our board unanimously rejected a $43 proposal last week so I'm a little confused by their strategy. With the board unanimously rejecting a $43 per share offer, I'm not sure what they're up to," Loewen told Reuters in an interview at the New York Stock Exchange.

Service Corp earlier announced it would offer Loewen shareholders $45 per share following the Loewen board's rejection of an unsolicited $43 per share offer. The new offer values the proposed transaction at nearly $3 billion.
Loewen declined to speak specifically about the bid. The company has advised shareholders to take no action.
"The board will be meeting in the next couple of weeks. We'll be responding to this proposal after that," he said.
Loewen was in New York to launch the trading of the company's stock on the New York Stock Exchange. U.S. shares previosuly had been traded on Nasdaq.
Despite being the target of a hopstile takeover, Loewen was able to remain lighthearted about the day's events. The company has said the NYSE move is important for its growth.

"To our knowledge, apparently our company is the only company that has had a hostile takeover bid on the hour that we were listed (for NYSE trading). So I guess that's just another chapter for my book," he said with a laugh.
Loewen is the second largest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries in North America. Service Corp is the largest.
Loewen also said the acquisition interest expressed by Service Corp has not come as a complete surprise.
"Service Corp has been interested in our company for many, many years. We've always known that they would be opportunistic given the chance, so in that context, it's not unexpected," he said.
Loewen later withdrew its statement about shareholders taking no action and said that it has not given any advice to its shareholders about the Service Corp bid.
Both companies have aggressively been buying privately-owned funeral homes, although Loewen claims to have a stronger track record than Service Corp.
"We see this platform we've been given as a result of Service Corp's hostile offer -- we see it as an opportunity to tell the Loewen growth story like never before," he said.
Loewen said the company received strong support from the indstry's private players at an industry conference last week in Florida.
He said that the company plans to continue its acquisition strategy amid industry consolidation. He said Loewen has a "handshake deal" on another acquisition, but declined to be more specific.
Loewen has signed acquisition pacts or closed transactions valued at more than $1.2 billion so far this year, far above its initial prediction of $500 million.

"I really think it's the tip of the iceberg," he said of the industry's consolidation. "I think it's huge. We're talking about a $15 to $20 billion revenue industry and only a couple of billion is consolidated today."
